upgrade: Integral Hasse principle for Markoff-type surfaces (FAILED upgrade: almost all, not every)

title: Reduction theory for ES solutions and congruence exclusion of all reduced representatives
connection: In Ghosh–Sarnak failures every orbit has a reduced representative in a bounded region, and congruence conditions can exclude all of them. ES: every solution has x ∈ (p/4, 3p/4] (x minimal); the 'reduced representatives' are the pairs (x, m = 4x − p). Ask whether congruence conditions modulo a fixed M can exclude all reduced representatives for infinitely many p (that would be a non-BM obstruction).
why: A concrete search space for genuinely new obstructions; if impossible for structural reasons, that fact is itself a (small) theorem.
first_step: For M = 840·k, compute which residues of p mod M admit a reduced representative whose two-term remainder is locally solvable mod M; check that no non-square class is fully excluded.
refs: arXiv:1706.06712 (Ghosh-Sarnak, Integral points on Markoff type cubic surfaces, Invent. Math. 229 (2022))
upgrade: Integral Hasse principle for Markoff-type surfaces (FAILED upgrade: almost all, not every)

title: Search for F_q[T] counterexamples to the direct ES analogue at small q
connection: Function-field analogues sometimes fail at small q (as Artin's C₂ fails for small p). If the direct analogue of ES over F_q[T] (with a suitable positivity replacement, e.g. degree constraints) fails for some small q, the failure mechanism is an explicit structure that ℤ-ES must avoid; if it holds for all tested q, the F_q[T] proof (repo) is the template.
why: Cheap exhaustive computation with high information value (8/131-type test in the function-field world).
first_step: For q = 2, 3, 4, 5 and irreducible P of degree ≤ 12, search solutions of 4/P = 1/X + 1/Y + 1/Z (with the repo's degree conventions) and list failures.
refs: Effinger-Hayes, Additive Number Theory of Polynomials over a Finite Field (1991)
upgrade: Function-field analogues (Goldbach over F_q[T], twin primes for large q)

title: Positive proportion before density one (Bourgain–Fuchs) for bounded-shape certificates
connection: Bourgain–Fuchs proved a positive proportion of integers are Apollonian curvatures before density one. For ES, bounded-shape certificate families (u, B ≤ U fixed) cover a positive proportion of primes by Dirichlet; quantify the proportion covered by shapes with u, B ≤ U as U grows, versus the full ES density one.
why: Measures how much of ES is 'explained' by bounded shapes (Mordell-type) vs growing ones — the shape-growth rate needed for density one.
first_step: Compute coverage of primes ≤ 10⁹ by (★) with u, B ≤ U for U = 1..100.
refs: arXiv:2307.02749 (Haag-Kertzer-Rickards-Stange, The local-global conjecture for Apollonian circle packings is false)

title: Lee–Yang / stability-preserver view of the window generating polynomial
connection: Lee–Yang (zeros on the unit circle for every ferromagnetic Ising model) and Borcea–Brändén stability preservers prove non-vanishing for every instance via polynomial stability. The window certificate count is a coefficient of Π_i (Σ_{|j|≤a_i} x^{j·g_i}) in the group ring; ask whether a multivariate stable polynomial encodes certificate existence so that stability forces a nonzero coefficient.
why: Stability/interlacing proved 'every instance' theorems where probabilistic arguments only gave typical instances.
first_step: Write the multivariate polynomial Π_i (1 + z_i + z_i^{-1}) with z_i ↦ characters; examine real-stability of natural specialisations for small examples.
refs: arXiv:1304.4132 (Marcus-Spielman-Srivastava, Interlacing families I: all degrees)
upgrade: Interlacing families: Ramanujan graphs of every degree; Kadison-Singer

title: Third-method insurance: find a family whose success is uncorrelated with both (★) and b=1
connection: Holowinsky–Soundararajan needed exactly two complementary methods. ES data show (★) ∪ b=1 never fail together ≤ 10⁸, but a proof-grade argument may need a third family whose success correlates with neither (e.g. ES₅, Type I lines, small windows). Measure correlations of success indicators among 6–8 families.
why: Identifies the minimal robust family set for a complementary-methods proof.
first_step: Compute the correlation matrix of family success indicators (and of their counts) over primes ≤ 10⁸ in Mordell-hard classes.
refs: arXiv:0809.1636 (Holowinsky-Soundararajan, Mass equidistribution for Hecke eigenforms)

title: Mordell's class-number formula for yz + zx + xy = p as an exact power-size count
connection: Duke/Iwaniec exploit class-number-sized representation counts. Mordell (1923) gives, for prime n, the number of positive solutions of yz + zx + xy = n as 3G(n) − 3 (G class-number type). ES solutions satisfy σ₂(x,y,z) = 4σ₃/p; scaling Type II solutions (y = pY, z = pZ) gives p·YZ = x(4YZ − Y − Z), a σ₂-type relation. Look for a bijection or injection from a subset of Mordell's solutions (power-many) to ES certificates.
why: Would tie ES to an exact class-number count (power-size, every p), the Duke template.
first_step: For small primes, list Mordell's solutions of yz + zx + xy = p (or = 4p, kp) and test which ones transform into ES solutions via simple rational maps.

title: Which almost-all ES results are sharp in the Kolmogorov sense?
connection: Kolmogorov's divergent Fourier series shows some a.e. theorems are optimal. For each ES-type almost-all theorem (single levels, (★), b=1, ES₅), decide whether infinitely many failures are known/expected (then the almost-all result is 'sharp') or not; only the latter are candidates for every-p upgrades.
why: Avoids attempting upgrades of statements that are actually false infinitely often (like single-level or (★)-only versions may be).
first_step: For each sub-route, estimate Σ_p P(fail) under the calibrated model; classify as 'expected finitely many' vs 'expected infinitely many' failures.
refs: Kolmogorov, Fund. Math. 4 (1923)/ C. R. 1926 (everywhere divergent L^1 Fourier series)
upgrade: Large values / Kolmogorov counterexample (a.e. cannot be upgraded)

title: Average over p of Schinzel-type events for the polynomials 4Cp + 1 in C
connection: Skorobogatov–Sofos average over polynomial families. At fixed p, the family {4Cp + 1 : C} is a linear polynomial in C; averaging over p (with C free) gives Schinzel-on-average-type statements on factorisations of 4Cp + 1 that underlie the almost-all ES theorem. Make explicit which 'Schinzel on average' input the almost-all proof uses and whether a pointwise-in-p version is a known open problem.
why: Locates ES exactly within the Schinzel-on-average landscape (what is averaged, over what).
first_step: Rewrite Vaughan's almost-all proof as a statement about factorisations of 4Cp + 1 averaged over p; identify the pointwise analogue.
refs: arXiv:2005.02998 (Skorobogatov-Sofos, Schinzel Hypothesis on average and rational points)
upgrade: Schinzel Hypothesis H for 100% of polynomials (stuck mirror)

title: Twists by characters mod 4C as 'twisted point counts' with an exactly known total
connection: Weil-type lower bounds use that twisted counts sum to an exact total. At level C, Σ_{χ mod 4C} χ(−1)·#{d | N : χ(d)…} expansions give D_C^−(N) = (1/φ(4C)) Σ_χ χ̄(−1) σ_χ(N) exactly; the trivial character gives τ(N)/φ(4C), others are twisted divisor sums. A lower bound needs |Σ_{χ ≠ 1} …| < τ(N): bound the twisted divisor sums σ_χ(N) pointwise (multiplicative, |σ_χ(q^a)| ≤ a + 1).
why: Pointwise bounds on σ_χ(N) are trivial-to-moderate; the issue is how many characters and how cancellation among them behaves for structured N = 4Cp + 1.
first_step: For hard p and small C, compute |Σ_{χ ≠ 1} χ̄(−1)σ_χ(N)| vs τ(N) and record how close it gets.

title: Kaplansky-type ternary forms with conditional (GRH) complete lists as structural analogues
connection: Beyond Ramanujan's form, several ternary forms have GRH-conditional complete lists of exceptions (Ono–Soundararajan type). Their exception lists are finite but sporadic; ES-adjacent statements with sporadic exceptions (U(n) list, b=1 failures) might be 'ternary-form-like'. Test whether the U(n)/b=1 exceptions are represented/non-represented by specific ternary forms.
why: A direct dictionary between sporadic ES-adjacent exceptions and ternary-form exceptions would import Waldspurger/GRH technology.
first_step: For the known sporadic exception lists, test representability by all reduced positive ternary forms of discriminant ≤ 500.
upgrade: Ramanujan's ternary form x^2+y^2+10z^2 (stuck at conditional)

title: Switching between the two cofactors of 4Cp + 1 and the two ES types
connection: Chen's switching replaces a hard count by a dual count where the roles of variables swap. In (★), 4Cp + 1 = (4uC − 1)(4BC − 1) is symmetric; the b=1 line uses p + 4d with a divisor ≡ −1 (mod 4d). Find an explicit bijection/switch between near-certificates of one line and of the other, so that an upper bound for near-misses of one yields a lower bound for hits of the other.
why: Switching is the concrete mechanism behind complementary-route arguments.
first_step: Search for maps (u, B, C) ↦ (d, w) between (★) data and b=1 data for the same p, and test on hard primes.

title: Zero-free region analogue: a range of levels where no 'conspiracy' is possible
connection: Linnik's theorem uses a zero-free region near s = 1 for all characters of modulus ≤ Q. For ES, find a range of small levels (C ≤ C₀(p)) where the relevant characters (mod 4C) are so few that a full conspiracy against certificates would force p into explicit square-like residue classes (contradiction for non-squares).
why: Small levels have few characters; a 'no conspiracy at small levels' lemma would be the ES zero-free region.
first_step: For C ≤ 30, characterise the residues of p (mod lcm(4C)) for which all these levels fail; compute the density of such residues and whether they are squares.

title: Box principle for windows: two windows with the same residue data combine
connection: Thue's lemma is a box principle. Pigeonhole windows e by the residue vector of p modulo small primes and the factorisation shape of N_e; two windows with equal data might combine (via CRT) into a certificate at the window e·e′ or at lcm, if a combination law exists.
why: Pigeonhole needs a combination law; windows have CRT structure that may supply one.
first_step: Test on data: for pairs of failing windows e, e′ with compatible data, check whether e·e′ (or another derived window) succeeds more often than random.
upgrade: Thue's lemma / pigeonhole for x^2 + y^2

title: Exact formulas for divisor-class counts: Ramanujan sums expansion of D_C^−(N)
connection: Rademacher-type exact expansions use Kloosterman/Ramanujan sums. The class-restricted divisor count D^−_{4C}(N) has an exact finite Fourier expansion over additive characters mod 4C (Ramanujan sums c_q(·)); for the all-level sum this becomes a series Σ_q c_q-type terms, an ES 'singular series' with exact tail.
why: An exact Ramanujan-sum expansion of R(p) separates the main (BM) part from the rest explicitly and may be summable in closed form at small q.
first_step: Write R(p) = Σ_q A_q(p) with A_q built from Ramanujan sums; compute A_q(p) numerically for q ≤ 100 and the remainder.
upgrade: Rademacher exact formula (asymptotic -> exact for every n)

title: Grunwald–Wang-type exceptions: when local prescriptions at 2 cannot be realised globally
connection: Shafarevich's 2-group case had a gap related to the Grunwald–Wang special case (local conditions at 2 not realisable globally). ES certificate conditions involve 4C and 8ℤ − p (2-adic structure). Check whether ES sub-routes have Grunwald–Wang-type 2-adic exceptions: residue patterns at 2 that are locally fine but globally unrealisable for certain p.
why: 2-adic subtleties are exactly where 'local implies global' historically failed in a structured way.
first_step: Analyse the 2-adic constraints in (★) and b=1 (C, d powers of 2, p mod 2^k) and test failures' residues mod 2^k.
refs: Neukirch-Schmidt-Wingberg, Cohomology of Number Fields, Ch. IX
upgrade: Shafarevich: every solvable group is a Galois group over Q

title: Commutator-style 'every element' from character ratios: target −1 in (ℤ/e)* via products of few divisor classes
connection: Ore-type results show every element is a product of few commutators using character bounds. Analogue for windows: when the prime-factor classes of N_e generate a large subgroup H ∋ −1, show −1 is a product of a bounded number of them (with ±1 exponents) using additive-combinatorics in abelian groups (Cauchy–Davenport/Kneser iterated), i.e. a bound on the 'diameter' of H w.r.t. the generating multiset.
why: Reduces window certificates to a diameter bound in a Cayley graph of an abelian group — fully finite and checkable.
first_step: Compute the ±1-diameter of (ℤ/e)* w.r.t. the multiset of prime-factor classes of N_e for hard (p, e), versus ω(N_e).
refs: arXiv:0904.4146? (Liebeck-O'Brien-Shalev-Tiep, The Ore conjecture, J. Eur. Math. Soc. 12 (2010))
upgrade: Ore conjecture / Waring problem for finite simple groups

title: Finite base + closure: what finite verification would an ES closure theorem need?
connection: Graham's 77-theorem needed a finite check (78–333) plus closure maps. If any closure/transfer system for ES certificates were found (see closure items), compute the minimal 'base' of verified instances it needs; ES is verified to 10¹⁸, so any closure system with base ≤ 10¹⁸ would finish.
why: Turns closure-map searches into a concrete success criterion.
first_step: For each candidate closure map found by search, compute the set of primes it reaches from primes ≤ 10⁶ and check whether its complement thins out.
refs: Graham, A theorem on partitions, J. Austral. Math. Soc. 3 (1963) 435-441 (77-theorem); see also Graham, Pacific J. Math. 10 (1960) 1221-1224 / OEIS A051882 (subagent dating conflict: check)
upgrade: Graham: every n > 77 is a sum of distinct integers with reciprocals summing to 1

title: Syracuse-type random variable for ES: the 2-adic/3-adic structure of minimal certificates
connection: Tao's Collatz proof analysed the distribution of a 3-adic 'Syracuse random variable'. ES certificates carry 2-adic data (4 | t; 8ℤ − p branch) and 3-adic data (Mordell classes mod 3). Define the analogous random variable (residues of minimal certificate parameters mod 2^k, 3^k) and study its distribution and mixing as p varies.
why: Fine-scale mixing of certificate residues is the kind of statement that powers almost-all → 'almost every scale' improvements.
first_step: Compute the distribution of minimal certificate parameters mod 2^k·3^j over primes ≤ 10⁸ and test for Fourier decay.
refs: arXiv:1909.03562 (Tao, Almost all orbits of the Collatz map attain almost bounded values)
upgrade: Collatz: almost all orbits attain almost bounded values (stuck mirror)

title: Linear recurrences for minimal certificates along exponential families
connection: SML-type structure suggests that along n_s = a·b^s + c the minimal certificate parameters may follow linear recurrences in s on residue classes of s. Detect such recurrences for the proved families (3·2^s + 1, 63·2^s + 1) and use them to predict certificates for open families.
why: Recurrences would give explicit every-s constructions (as Niederreiter for Zaremba).
first_step: Run Berlekamp–Massey on sequences of minimal (u, B, C) along proved families restricted to s in fixed classes.

title: Reducibility check automation: verify 'configuration ⇒ certificate' lemmas by computer
connection: The four-colour proof verified each configuration's reducibility by computer. For ES, configuration lemmas of the form 'if p ≡ r (mod M) and 4Cp + 1 has factorisation pattern π then a certificate exists' can be verified symbolically for each (r, π); automate generation and checking of such lemmas.
why: Builds a library of machine-checked partial results that any case-analysis proof would need.
first_step: Implement a checker that, given (M, r, C, pattern), decides via CRT whether a certificate is forced; run over small M and patterns.

title: Stickiness analogue: certificates at nearby levels share prime factors
connection: Wang–Zahl handled 'sticky' Kakeya sets where tubes cluster coherently across scales. For fixed p, near-certificates at levels C and C + kq share the prime q (CRT); study whether certificate data are 'sticky' across levels (coherent families sharing primes) and whether non-sticky configurations are easier to force.
why: A structural dichotomy (sticky vs non-sticky) that may split the problem into two tractable halves.
first_step: Measure, for fixed p, the clustering of certificate-bearing levels modulo primes dividing their divisors.
refs: arXiv:2502.17655 (Wang-Zahl, Volume estimates for unions of convex sets, and the Kakeya set conjecture in three dimensions)

title: Limit objects of normalised divisor-class data as p → ∞ (Sendov's limiting measures)
connection: Tao's Sendov proof studies limiting zero distributions. For ES, attach to p the empirical measure of (log d / log N, class of d mod 4C) over levels C ≤ K and divisors d of 4Cp + 1; study its limit as p → ∞ (should be a product of uniform measures) and the rate; a counterexample sequence would converge to a measure avoiding a fixed 'certificate region'.
why: Gives a concrete limit object for compactness arguments.
first_step: Compute these empirical measures for p ~ 10⁶, 10⁸, 10¹⁰ and measure distance to the product-uniform model.
refs: arXiv:2012.04125 (Tao, Sendov's conjecture for sufficiently high degree polynomials)
